slides.title: How to answer *relatives' questions*
slides.sub: Shaadi kab? Salary kitni? Good news kab? Bua ji has them ready. Krishna had one answer.

slides.title: Three questions. *One party.*
slides.body: "Shaadi kab?" "Salary kitni?" "Good news kab?" Asked in front of everyone, between the sweets and the crackers. Your face goes hot.

slides.iast: mātrā-sparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ, āgamāpāyino 'nityās tāṁs titikṣasva bhārata
slides.meaning: Touches of the world bring cold and heat, joy and pain. They come and go and don't last, so bear them, Arjuna.

slides.title: The *key words*, simply
slides.body: Mātrā-sparśa: what touches your senses. Śītoṣṇa: cold and heat. Āgamāpāyin: they come and go. Titikṣasva: bear it calmly, without hitting back.

slides.title: Said on a *battlefield*
slides.body: The text says Krishna told this to Arjuna just before the Mahabharata war, when Arjuna was too upset to fight. One of his first lessons: hard moments pass.

slides.title: Relatives' questions are *weather*
slides.body: For us today: Bua ji's question lasts ten seconds. Like a cold wind, let it pass. You don't owe every question a full answer.

slides.title: Screenshot these *replies*
slides.body: Shaadi kab? — "You'll get the first card." Salary kitni? — "Enough for your gift!" Good news kab? — "Kaju katli first!" Then smile and change the topic.

slides.kicker: Before you leave for the party
slides.title: Save it. *Send it* to your cousin.
slides.sub: Bua ji will ask again at the next wedding. Send this to the cousin going to the same party. Follow @sutraverselife for real-life lessons from ancient wisdom.
